newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks weaker in London trading.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks weaker in London trading.

text.p: Japanese stocks were weaker in London on Wednesday amid selective profit-taking, traders said.
They said dealers who had followed Wall Street's rise in recent weeks were offloading their holdings aggressively.
"We're a bit weaker. There has been aggressive selling in stocks like Toyota and Honda that have performed well over the past weeks," one trader said.

By 1500 GMT, London's Nikkei ISE 50 index was down 8.83 points to 1497.59. In Tokyo, the key Nikkei-225 index closed down 72.97 points at 21,345.28 after the Bank of Japan released "tankan" business sentiment data in line with expectations.
Toyota slipped in London trade to 3135 yen from a Tokyo close of 3140 yen. Honda Motor slid to 3440 yen in London after closing in Tokyo at a record high of 3470 yen.
"Trading today is merely profit-taking in select shares," a trader said. "The rest of the market is still low volume."
Sony Corp closed at a record high of 7380 yen in Tokyo but traded at 7362.5 yen in London.
